transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi… thank you. I guess what finally made me come in is, well, it’s not anything huge, but I keep forgetting little things I usually handle fine—like returning calls, turning in a registration form, or remembering to stop for an errand on my way home. It’s starting to feel a little embarrassing, and I thought maybe I should ask about it before it gets worse.
How long have you been noticing these memory problems?

I think it’s been more noticeable since I started my evening certificate program… so, about 15 months ago. I mean, I probably managed okay before, but since then it’s just been harder to keep track of things. Does that make sense?
Are these memory problems interfering with your work or daily activities?

A little, yes. I mean, I’m still getting by overall, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is… but I’ve missed some small follow-ups at work, and a few school deadlines, enough times that I’m starting to worry people might think I’m careless. I’d really like to move toward an Office Manager role eventually, and I don’t want this to hurt my reputation, if that makes sense.
Have you been feeling anxious or depressed about these memory issues?

I don’t think so… not in a serious way. I mean, I get a little frustrated with myself when I forget something, and maybe embarrassed, but I wouldn’t say I’m depressed or really anxious. It’s more like, “Why can’t I just keep on top of this?” if that makes sense.
Have you had any head injuries or been in an accident recently?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t been in any accident or had a head injury recently, at least nothing that I can think of.
Do you have trouble focusing or paying attention to tasks?

Yes… I do, somewhat. I mean, I can focus, especially if it’s quiet, but at the office or in class, little things can pull me away—like a phone ringing, people talking nearby, or even just a random thought about something I need to do at home. Then I realize I’ve lost track of what I was working on. I don’t want to overstate it, but it does happen.
Do you ever find that your thoughts are disjointed or hard to follow?

Um… I don’t think so, not really. I mean, sometimes I lose my train of thought or have to back up and remember what I was saying, but I wouldn’t say my thoughts are disjointed or hard to follow. At least, I hope they don’t come across that way.
Do you find it difficult to express your thoughts in a coherent and logical manner?

I don’t think so, not in a major way. I mean, sometimes I might take a second to find the right words, but I usually feel like I can explain what I mean. If I’m not making sense, I’d want someone to tell me, but I haven’t really noticed that being a big problem.
Do you find it harder to learn new things than you used to?

I’m not sure I’d say it’s harder than it used to be. I mean, I can learn new things if I’m shown clearly or I can take notes. Sometimes it takes me a bit to get into it, but I haven’t really noticed a big change, if that makes sense.
Do you ever feel mentally foggy or like you're in a daze?

Not really, no. I mean, I have moments where I’m tired or kind of not fully focused, but I wouldn’t describe it as being in a daze. I don’t think that’s a big issue for me… unless you mean something more specific?
Do you often feel tired?
I wouldn’t say often, no. I mean, I get tired like anyone does, especially after a long day, but it’s not something I’d call unusual or a major problem. Is that the kind of tired you mean?
Do you find that your daily life or workspace is more disorganized than it used to be?

A little, yeah. I mean, I can usually keep up at work, so I don’t want to make it sound like everything’s a mess. But since I started evening classes, my desk and my class folder kind of turn into piles, and even my email reminders get cluttered. Then I spend time just trying to figure out what I’m supposed to do first, which is frustrating. I’m not sure if that counts as disorganized, but it has been more noticeable.
Do you often find yourself struggling to find the right words when speaking?

Not really, I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes I’ll pause to think of the best way to say something, but I haven’t noticed myself constantly losing words or anything like that. I hope that makes sense.
Do you have trouble recalling specific words or names when trying to remember them?

Not especially, no. I mean, everyone blanks on a name once in a while, but I haven’t noticed it being a real problem for me. If I pause, it’s usually just me trying to be clear, I think. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you have trouble planning out your day or tasks in advance?

Some, yes. I can usually manage if it’s just work, and I don’t want to overstate it, but since adding evening classes it’s gotten harder to plan ahead. My desk and class folder kind of become piles, and my email reminders pile up too, so I’ll waste time trying to decide what I’m supposed to do first. I do get it done eventually, but it’s not as smooth as I’d like.
Do you find that you often forget information you've recently learned?

I don’t think so, not often. If it’s something I just learned, I can usually remember it okay, especially if I’ve written it down or it was explained clearly. I might need a reminder here and there, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly forgetting new information. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
Do you find it hard to make decisions?

Sometimes, yes—but more in the “what should I do first?” kind of way. I can usually keep up at work, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Since I started evening classes, though, my desk, class folder, and email reminders all sort of turn into piles, and then I waste time deciding what I’m supposed to tackle first. Does that count as trouble making decisions?
Do you have trouble initiating tasks or projects on your own?

A little, yes. I mean, I do start things eventually, but if it’s something like reading a long chapter for class or writing out a plan, I tend to put it off. Then it gets late and I’m rushing through it after work, which I know isn’t ideal. I’m not trying to avoid it completely, it’s just hard to make myself sit down and begin sometimes.
Do you feel like your mind gets tired more easily than it used to?

Maybe a little? I wouldn’t say my mind gets tired all the time, but when something takes a lot of sitting and focusing—like reading a long chapter or writing out a plan—I notice I keep putting it off. Then it gets late after work and I’m rushing, which probably makes it feel more draining than it should. Is that the kind of mental tiredness you mean?
Do you find yourself getting distracted easily by your surroundings?

Yes, I do, though I try not to let it show too much. At the office or in class, if a phone rings or people are talking nearby, I can lose my place in what I was doing. Sometimes it’s not even noise—just a random thought about something at home, and then I realize I’ve drifted off. I usually get back to it, but it does pull me away.
